text:
ishaan: quick sync — I'm prototyping a delegated signing service that mint ephemeral x509 certs for internal services. main goals: avoid giving raw KMS sign rights to every service, have PoP (proof-of-possession) checks, and preserve strong audit trails across regions.
maria: OK curious — what's the flow? service -> signing svc -> KMS sign?
ishaan: exactly. service presents CSR + short-lived token bound to service identity. signing svc validates token and PoP, then calls KMS asymmetricSign with a dedicated key. returns cert chain.
jen: question on RBAC: what principals need access to the KMS key? only the signing svc's service account, right?
ishaan: yes that's the plan. signing svc SA has kms:AsymmetricSign. No other SA. services only get ephemeral certs from signing svc.
tarek: what about multi-region? do we replicate the signing key or run signing svc per-region?
ishaan: prefer per-region signing svc with locally-replicated keys (KMS multi-region keys or cross-region keys). avoids egress latency and single point of failure.
maria: audit requirements — we need per-request key usage logs with caller identity and CSR thumbprint. Also include the ephemeral cert serial in logs for revocation mapping.
jen: agree. We should record: signing_svc_sa, original_service_identity, csr_sha256, cert_serial, valid_from, valid_to, and request_headers (x-forwarded-for).
ishaan: can the KMS provide that level of metadata? many clouds only expose key operation logs (Sign called by signing-svc). We need an application layer audit to attach CSR thumbprint and service identity.
arek: (opsbot): deployment note — make sure the signing svc logs are forwarded to central audit cluster with immutability and TTL 13 months.
tarek: also need to ensure logs are signed or HMACed to prevent tampering before ingest.
jen: PoP checks — how strict? the service could prove possession of the private key used to generate CSR via a challenge. do we want that or is mTLS handshake enough?
ishaan: prefer challenge flow for first issuance and shorter tokens for rotation. sample flow: service requests a nonce from signing svc, signs it locally with its key, returns signed nonce + CSR + identity token.
maria: for rotation/compromise: if signing key is compromised, we need immediate revocation list and emergency rollout. plan?
jen: plan: 1) rotate signing key in KMS (create new key version and update signing svc), 2) publish CRL / OCSP responder update (signing svc maintains short-lived certs so CRL window small), 3) issue override to services to reject certs signed by old key based on cert issuer serial.
ishaan: we also need region failover: if primary region's signing svc is offline, fallback to secondary region but only if its KMS key is a known active key version. audits must record which region issued the cert.
tarek: regulatory ask — some customers require HSM-backed keys in specific geo. we need mapping of customer tenancy -> allowed signing regions. enforce via signing policy config and rejection of requests outside allowed regions.
maria: can we enforce PoP with KMS-bound attestation? e.g., require a token that KMS can verify? Feels tricky.
jen: alternative: use short-lived mTLS client certs for services that run in-host (created by workloads) and let workload orchestrator (kube) do proof via node attestations. outside-kube services must do challenge flow.
ishaan: here's a sample policy snippet I drafted to attach to the signing svc SA:```json
{ "bindings": [ {"role": "roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier", "members": ["serviceAccount:project:signing-svc-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"] } ], "condition": { "title": "region-restriction", "description": "only allow calls from signing-svc in allowed regions", "expression": "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/locations/us-')" } }
```
maria: looks good. Need an additional condition for keyVersion and an allowlist check.
jen: risk: CVE-2026-000X disclosed in some crypto lib that affects CSR parsing. we should add a quick-fix: sanitize/parsing layer and drop unsupported extensions before signing.
ishaan: noted — we'll add fuzz tests and a small sanitizer that strips crazy ASN.1 sequences.
security-bot: alert: recent scan found an S3 bucket with staging CSR artifacts open to internal devs. recommend immediate ACL update.
tarek: thanks security-bot — I've restricted the bucket and kicked an audit job.
maria: for incident playbook: 1) revoke signing key version in KMS 2) patch signing svc & rotate 3) update CRL/OCSP 4) alert customers and run cert inventory to identify affected certs 5) roll short-lived certs with new signer.
jen: add step to freeze admin SA keys and run RBAC audit to ensure no extra principals have AsymmetricSign.
ishaan: one more operational ask: expose metric 'sign_requests_total{region, tenant, result}' and 'sign_latency_ms' and 'sign_audit_exported' boolean so SRE can validate audit copy.
maria: and add a prometheus alert if audit_exported==false for >5 minutes.
jen: sounds actionable. can someone own sprint ticket?
ishaan: I'll open RFC + implementation ticket and assign initial spike. adding documents with design + PoP protocol details.
tarek: I'll follow up with infra on KMS multi-region replication constraints.
maria: I'll draft audit schema and CRL/OCSP integration notes.
jen: thanks all.
ishaan: tagging next steps: @maria @tarek @jen — can we sync tomorrow 10am PT?
opsbot: meeting created: "Signing svc design sync" 10:00 PT tomorrow — attendees: ishaan, maria, jen, tarek. :calendar:
